summary: Full v2 regression: USASpending gov contract intel, Risk score, 3-method Target price, batched Claude w/ 24h cache. 16/16 new pytest cases pass. Frontend dashboard renders Risk + Target columns, gold/amber gov signal badges (CONTRACT_SURGE/NEW_WINNER/MOMENTUM_STACK), Government Contracts panel, Budget Surges panel, GOV SCAN + RUN SCAN NOW buttons. All 7 new Telegram commands (/contracts, /scan_gov, /agency, /watchlist_contracts, /risk, /target, /compare) processed without crash (verified via activity_log entries). Token efficiency confirmed: 2nd scan run reports claude_calls_made=0 with claude_cache_hits == pre_filter_passed (11/11). Gov signals firing on expected tickers (LDOS, BAH, SAIC, LHX, DELL) — schema matches v2 spec.

minor.issue: Endpoint is unauthenticated and triggers real Claude tokens + Telegram blasts on every call. Acceptable for admin MVP but worth a rate-limit / shared-secret in production.

Risk score for LDOS came back negative (-1) with single positive factor '4+ agencies winning [-]'. Negative score still maps to LOW but mathematically odd; consider clamping score >= 0 before threshold mapping.

SAIC blended target shows +343.8% upside on dashboard — flagged in Claude thesis itself ('blended target appears anomalous'). Suggests contract_revenue_multiple method should be capped or weighted lower when revenue mismatch is extreme.

issues: Target column shows extreme upside numbers (+343%, +172%) without visual de-emphasis — could mislead users; consider amber/red coloring when blended deviates >2x from analyst consensus

action_items: Consider clamping risk score floor at 0 in compute_risk (/app/backend/services/risk_target.py)
Cap or down-weight contract_revenue_multiple target method when ratio vs analyst consensus exceeds e.g. 2x to avoid wildly off blended targets (SAIC +343%, LDOS +172%)
Optional: rate-limit /api/scan/run to prevent accidental Claude token burn and Telegram spam
critical_code_review_comments: scanner.run_scan: single batched Claude call confirmed working (claude_calls_made=1 on first run with 11 candidates). Cache key (ticker, date_key) hits 100% on subsequent same-day runs — solid token-efficiency design.

server.py /api/risk and /api/target each call fetch_fundamentals separately — for /compare endpoint they are gathered in parallel (good) but /risk → /target consecutive calls do not share fundamentals. Minor latency issue only.

telegram_service.handle_update logs every command via log_activity (verified) — webhook returns 200 even when handler raises async exceptions in BackgroundTasks. Consider surfacing handler failures to logs explicitly.
risk_target.compute_risk allows negative score (observed -1 for LDOS). Threshold logic still classifies as LOW so user-visible behaviour is fine, but score field semantically should be 0..N.
USASpending name_to_ticker is a static map — any new public-company contractor not in the map is silently dropped. Acceptable for v2 but worth documenting.
Dashboard.jsx target column numerator uses raw target_blended without bounds check; when methods diverge (e.g. SAIC 343%), no visual warning. Add color tier or warning icon when |upside| > 100%.
test_credentials: N/A — no auth in this app
seed_data_creation: Frontend test added+removed TSLA in watchlist. 7 Telegram cmd activity_log entries created (harmless, used for verification). No /scan/run was triggered beyond the single token-efficiency check (which hit cache, claude_calls_made=0).
context_for_next_testing_agent: v2 schema fully verified. Latest scan has 11 results: LDOS, BAH, SAIC, DUOL, LHX, DELL, SOC, NRIX, TWST, PRCH, CAR. Cache for today is hot — re-running /api/scan/run will return claude_calls_made=0 deterministically. Public URL: https://stock-scout-bot.preview.emergentagent.com. Keep an eye on the SAIC/LDOS extreme target % values — these come from contract_revenue_multiple method amplifying when small-cap has many contracts.
rca of the issue: No blocking bugs. Minor anomaly: risk score may go negative due to '4+ agencies winning' subtracting without floor; target blended occasionally extreme when contract_revenue_multiple diverges from analyst_consensus. Both are cosmetic/UX concerns, not functional failures.
